title: Grateful Dead Live at Yasgur's Farm on 1969-08-16

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of the chaotic Woodstock set with an epic 45‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight, but the performance is uneven and technically troubled.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that conveys both the historic ambience of Woodstock and the on‑stage technical hiccups – microphone feedback, power outages and electronic hum are audible, yet several reviewers praise its clarity and strong audience presence. Musically the show swings between typical Dead fare (a brief Dark Star) and standout moments like Pigpen’s nearly 40‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight, though some feel the set is disjointed and marred by the band’s frustration.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is judged average to mixed (typical set, technical mishaps) while recording quality is generally praised as good/excellent despite noted interference; weighting yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear capture of the stage with strong audience mix, but plagued by microphone feedback, power outages and electronic hum that create occasional muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A fairly typical Dead set for the era, hampered by on‑stage technical chaos; the first half is uneven while the second half shines with an extended Lovelight that many fans cite as the highlight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His playing is noted as being affected by mic issues (an ungrounded microphone incident) but no specific praise or criticism of his guitar tone.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen leads a nearly 40‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight, praised for its energy by some reviewers and criticized for poor sound quality by others.
